questions.question: The displacement of a particle at time $t$ second is $s = 2t^{3}-3t^{2}+5t-4$ metre. Find (i) its velocity and acceleration when $t=2$ second, and (ii) whether the particle is ever momentarily at rest.
questions.solution:
**Velocity** is $\dfrac{ds}{dt}$ and **acceleration** is $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=\dfrac{d^{2}s}{dt^{2}}$.

**(i)**
$$v=\frac{ds}{dt}=6t^{2}-6t+5$$
$$a=\frac{dv}{dt}=12t-6$$
At $t=2$ second:
$$v=6(4)-6(2)+5=24-12+5=17\ \text{m/s}$$
$$a=12(2)-6=18\ \text{m/s}^{2}$$

**(ii)** The particle is at rest when $v=0$:
$$6t^{2}-6t+5=0$$
The discriminant is
$$\Delta=(-6)^{2}-4(6)(5)=36-120=-84<0$$
There is no real root, so **the particle is never at rest**. (Confirmation: $v$ has its least value at $t=\frac{6}{2\times 6}=\frac12$, where $v=6(0.25)-3+5=3.5>0$ m/s.)
questions.knowledgeNote: If $v=0$ has a negative discriminant the particle never stops; alternatively check $v$ at the vertex of the quadratic.
